dedupe_keys.name: nodal demand profile for ghana 2024 107 buses x 8 760 hours

description: This data set is a synthetic hourly demand profile for every bus of a Ghana power grid model for 2024, filling the gap left by the lack of public substation load data in many developing countries. It was published on Zenodo in June 2026 by Douglas Koomson, Richard Asiamah and Daniel Molzahn. It is a matrix of 107 buses by 8,760 hours, built for the third version of the MATPOWER Ghana synthetic grid, and is designed for steady-state power system research, reliability analysis and expansion planning. The profile matches the monthly national energy consumption, 23,701.46 GWh in total, and localised monthly peak demands reported by the Ghana Energy Commission in its national energy outlooks, and maps system totals to buses through nodal participation factors so that demand stays consistent while network limits are respected. Coverage is Ghana's grid at bus level. Files are a MATLAB file and a CSV, downloadable from Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: loads are synthetic allocations, not metered substation data, and the profile is tied to one grid model version. Simulation uses are time-series power flow, reliability and expansion studies on the Ghana test grid. Related records: data-synthetic-electric-grid-ghana is the grid model it fits.
